newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close shade up on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close shade up on local buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed marginally up on Monday as profit-taking slowed the momentum created by local buying by big institutional investors, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.15 points higher at 628.05. Price gains outnumbered declines 25 to 23. Ceylon Brewery rose 1.75 rupees to 39 and Korea Ceylon Footwear, 1.50 to 19.50.
"A couple of very big local institutions are taking long-term positions, which is cushioning the fall caused by profit-taking," said Shafi Waheed, a trader at brokerage CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
Turnover was 58.9 million rupees on 1.2 million shares. The main trades were 251,300 Dipped Products at 85 rupees.
Foreign buying was 5.3 million rupees, while selling amounted to 22.2 million.
Local buying, which has taken the index up four percent so far this year, has been led by the state-owned Bank of Ceylon and Employees Trust Fund (ETF), a statutory gratuity fund.
"The ETF is not in the market to prop it up. We are using the current low prices to take long-term positions," said Densil Guneratne, chairman of the fund.
